operator_io_quirks: All table/column names are backtick-quoted in DDL; mixed case (Course_Authors_and_Tutors, Student_Course_Enrolment) — must preserve original spelling and double-quote in generated SQL.
DDL uses backticks; sqlite_master stores them verbatim — CREATE TABLE replay must keep backticks or re-quote.
Student_Tests_Taken has NO primary key (pk=[]); sample_fresh_primary_keys must no-op on empty PK, and drop_unique_duplicates has no unique columns to check.

Student_Tests_Taken.registration_id is a FK to Student_Course_Enrolment.registration_id but is NOT unique in the child (distinct 10 of 15 rows) — many-to-one, not 1:1; FK fill draws with replacement from parent's final values.
All DATETIME columns store TEXT 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' (space separator, 19 chars); ts_fuzzer dispatches to Date (first element not int-parsable) — Date template must be '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'.

date_of_registration/date_of_latest_logon are nullable DATETIME but null_rate 0.0; date_of_enrolment/date_of_completion/date_test_taken are NOT NULL DATETIME — TS does not enforce NOT NULL, so insert failures will be skipped.

VARCHAR(n) declared types dispatch to String with length=n (e.g. VARCHAR(3) author_tutor_ATB, VARCHAR(1) gender_mf, VARCHAR(10) password) — String length range [min len, max len+1] from elements, not from declared n.
author_tutor_ATB VARCHAR(3) holds 3-digit numeric strings ('331','975') — String fuzzer will treat as int-like and add +-1 variants; storage text.
gender_mf VARCHAR(1) has only 2 distinct values ('0','1') — String fuzzer with tiny element set; contamination will produce implausible genders.
test_result VARCHAR(255) has only 2 distinct values ('Pass','Fail') — String fuzzer will contaminate; ENUM-like but not declared.
course_name and course_description have identical sample values (both 'database','advanced database',...) — likely COPY/FD relationship in original; TS treats independently.
Small tables (3–20 rows); original_values sampling k=min(5,len) means Subjects gets all 3 values, others 5 of 15/20.
operator_ts_expectations: Date fuzzer with template '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S' on all 5 DATETIME columns; range from min/max of 5 sampled originals (e.g. Students ~2015-07..2018-03), so fresh dates cluster in that window — plausible for date_of_registration but implausible for date_of_latest_logon (should be later).
Number fuzzer on all INTEGER PKs and FK columns: range [-10^scale,10^scale] with scale=4 default (no args) → values up to 10000, far beyond original 1..20; PKs will be huge and sparse.

FK columns (Courses.author_id, Courses.subject_id, Student_Course_Enrolment.student_id/course_id, Student_Tests_Taken.registration_id) draw from parent's final values with replacement — ties/duplicates guaranteed, which is correct for many-to-one but may over-produce duplicates vs original distinct counts.

String fuzzer on login_name/password/personal_name/family_name etc. produces random CHARSET strings with 50% contamination — implausible names, but original also has random-looking passwords (hex) so password columns may be OK.
String fuzzer on gender_mf (VARCHAR(1), 2 elements) will emit random 1-char strings and contaminated variants — implausible gender values → likely FN on gender filters.
String fuzzer on test_result (2 elements) will emit random strings — implausible Pass/Fail → FN on test_result='Pass' queries.
String fuzzer on subject_name (3 elements: 'Computer Science','Arts','Language') will contaminate — FN on subject_name filters.
course_name/course_description treated independently by TS → COPY/FD between them broken → FP on queries joining/equating them.
Date fuzzer p-inversion: p=0.2 default means element returned w.p. 0.2, fresh date w.p. 0.8 — fresh dates dominate; with max_l0 cap (0.5 prob, rng*30) reuse kicks in for larger tables.
Number fuzzer list_max quirk: upper end overwritten with full-range max → fresh draws span [-10000,10000] even when elements are 1..20; PKs and FKs will be implausible magnitudes.

NOT NULL columns (author_id, subject_id, date_of_enrolment, date_of_completion, date_test_taken, registration_id) — TS may emit NULLs from empty parent or String allow_none; those rows fail insert and are skipped, shrinking tables.
No PK on Student_Tests_Taken → no PK dedup; drop_unique_duplicates no-op → duplicate rows possible (original has 15 rows, 10 distinct registration_id, so duplicates already exist).
